comparisons.name: note 131 text
comparisons.expected: Definition. Values a single incisive question above many routine, unquestioned answers.
comparisons.actual: Definition. Values a single incisive question above many routine, unquestioned answers.

comparisons.name: note 317 text
comparisons.expected: Reflection. Distinguishes the difficulty of leaving a place from the greater difficulty of leaving its lingering influence.
comparisons.actual: Reflection. Distinguishes the difficulty of leaving a place from the greater difficulty of leaving its lingering influence.

comparisons.name: note 324 text
comparisons.expected: Reflection. Distinguishes authority's power to command obedience from its inability to command truth.
comparisons.actual: Reflection. Distinguishes authority's power to command obedience from its inability to command truth.

comparisons.name: note 342 text
comparisons.expected: Definition. Places the burden of proof on whoever asserts universal guilt.
comparisons.actual: Definition. Places the burden of proof on whoever asserts universal guilt.

comparisons.name: note 352 text
comparisons.expected: Definition. Traces morality's origin to the practical requirements of cooperation rather than to revelation.
comparisons.actual: Definition. Traces morality's origin to the practical requirements of cooperation rather than to revelation.

comparisons.name: note 385 text
comparisons.expected: Context. Rejects simple, fixed judgments of human nature as either wholly good or wholly corrupt.
comparisons.actual: Context. Rejects simple, fixed judgments of human nature as either wholly good or wholly corrupt.

comparisons.name: note 401 text
comparisons.expected: Context. Warns that treating belief as settled knowledge makes honest questioning harder to sustain.
comparisons.actual: Context. Warns that treating belief as settled knowledge makes honest questioning harder to sustain.

comparisons.name: note 404 text
comparisons.expected: Definition. Reframes doubt as a possible doorway to understanding, echoing Seeker 18:2's treatment of doubt meeting certainty.
comparisons.actual: Definition. Reframes doubt as a possible doorway to understanding, echoing Seeker 18:2's treatment of doubt meeting certainty.

comparisons.name: note 421 text
comparisons.expected: Definition. Notes that ideas and stories, not force alone, are often the true source of power.
comparisons.actual: Definition. Notes that ideas and stories, not force alone, are often the true source of power.

comparisons.name: note 424 text
comparisons.expected: Clarification. Justifies examining every narrative on the grounds of its power, not its worthlessness.
comparisons.actual: Clarification. Justifies examining every narrative on the grounds of its power, not its worthlessness.

comparisons.name: note 431 text
comparisons.expected: Reflection. Requires claims of divine approval to face the same scrutiny as any other claim, echoing Seeker 11:1.
comparisons.actual: Reflection. Requires claims of divine approval to face the same scrutiny as any other claim, echoing Seeker 11:1.

comparisons.name: note 441 text
comparisons.expected: Reflection. Distinguishes mere difference from superiority, tracing many injustices to their conflation.
comparisons.actual: Reflection. Distinguishes mere difference from superiority, tracing many injustices to their conflation.

comparisons.name: note 472 text
comparisons.expected: Reflection. Frames honesty as the condition love requires to grow, echoing Society 16:1’s treatment of truth.
comparisons.actual: Reflection. Frames honesty as the condition love requires to grow, echoing Society 16:1’s treatment of truth.

comparisons.name: note 735 text
comparisons.expected: Reflection. Lists trust and cooperation as requirements for a healthy society that are rarely formally assessed.
comparisons.actual: Reflection. Lists trust and cooperation as requirements for a healthy society that are rarely formally assessed.

comparisons.name: note 745 text
comparisons.expected: Clarification. Distinguishes religion's pursuit of faith from education's pursuit of understanding.
comparisons.actual: Clarification. Distinguishes religion's pursuit of faith from education's pursuit of understanding.

comparisons.name: note 778 text
comparisons.expected: Clarification. Distinguishes history reduced to recollection from history that cultivates genuine understanding.
comparisons.actual: Clarification. Distinguishes history reduced to recollection from history that cultivates genuine understanding.

comparisons.name: note 783 text
comparisons.expected: Definition. Notes that beliefs often survive long after their origins have been forgotten.
comparisons.actual: Definition. Notes that beliefs often survive long after their origins have been forgotten.

comparisons.name: note 791 text
comparisons.expected: Context. Notes that political, religious, and national movements often seek legitimacy through appeals to history.
comparisons.actual: Context. Notes that political, religious, and national movements often seek legitimacy through appeals to history.

comparisons.name: note 835 text
comparisons.expected: Reflection. Requires responsibility to follow wherever a choice is actually made, not only where visibility exists.
comparisons.actual: Reflection. Requires responsibility to follow wherever a choice is actually made, not only where visibility exists.

comparisons.name: note 853 text
comparisons.expected: Reflection. Notes that fewer people examine their own contribution to a society's corruption than examine society's corruption itself.
comparisons.actual: Reflection. Notes that fewer people examine their own contribution to a society's corruption than examine society's corruption itself.

comparisons.name: note 869 text
comparisons.expected: Definition. Distinguishes inherited categories, garments, from the self they are placed upon.
comparisons.actual: Definition. Distinguishes inherited categories, garments, from the self they are placed upon.

comparisons.name: note 890 text
comparisons.expected: Definition. Distinguishes geography's account of where something exists from its silence about what it becomes.
comparisons.actual: Definition. Distinguishes geography's account of where something exists from its silence about what it becomes.

comparisons.name: note 898 text
comparisons.expected: Reflection. Frames daily habits, such as greetings and obligations, as ongoing lessons in culture.
comparisons.actual: Reflection. Frames daily habits, such as greetings and obligations, as ongoing lessons in culture.

comparisons.name: note 906 text
comparisons.expected: Reflection. Observes that ideas and stories now travel faster than merchants or armies once did.
comparisons.actual: Reflection. Observes that ideas and stories now travel faster than merchants or armies once did.

comparisons.name: note 922 text
comparisons.expected: Reflection. Values self-understanding above the defense of an inherited label.
comparisons.actual: Reflection. Values self-understanding above the defense of an inherited label.

comparisons.name: note 938 text
comparisons.expected: Reflection. Recommends observing action over speech as the more reliable indicator of actual belief.
comparisons.actual: Reflection. Recommends observing action over speech as the more reliable indicator of actual belief.

comparisons.name: note 962 text
comparisons.expected: Reflection. Contrasts respect pursued through appearance with respect earned through character.
comparisons.actual: Reflection. Contrasts respect pursued through appearance with respect earned through character.

comparisons.name: note 1144 text
comparisons.expected: Clarification. Reframes the central question as one of underlying motive rather than the specific action taken.
comparisons.actual: Clarification. Reframes the central question as one of underlying motive rather than the specific action taken.

comparisons.name: note 1300 text
comparisons.expected: Definition. Notes that no market survives without willing participants, including the audience that sustains a performer.
comparisons.actual: Definition. Notes that no market survives without willing participants, including the audience that sustains a performer.

comparisons.name: note 1366 text
comparisons.expected: Definition. Distinguishes desiring transformation from desiring the discipline required to produce it.
comparisons.actual: Definition. Distinguishes desiring transformation from desiring the discipline required to produce it.

comparisons.name: note 1467 text
comparisons.expected: Definition. Locates human worth as independent of brand, status, or public approval.
comparisons.actual: Definition. Locates human worth as independent of brand, status, or public approval.

detail.rawReportText:
Punctuation kept exactly as printed (possible typos, not corrected)

- `?;` in Inquiry 31:6 ("a life?; every"), Freedom 28:7 ("collapse?; these"), Identity 7:1 ("they are?; many")
- `.".` (full stop after a closing quotation) in Inquiry 32:3, 34:4, 39:13, Freedom 34:2, Society 41:12, and `?"; … ?".` in Identity 13:29/14:29
- Quotation marks and apostrophes are mixed: straight `'` and `"` alongside curly `’ “ ”`. Each is kept as printed.
- Dashes: verses mostly use an unspaced em dash (`word—word`). Notes mostly use a spaced one (`word — word`). Both are kept.

repeatedPassages.text: Many defend the ways of their fathers; few ask whether their fathers were correct.
Count not heads before examining reasons; the crowd often follows confidence; wisdom follows evidence.
Victory over pride is greater than victory over enemies; for the enemy outside may retreat.
Pride within returns every morning; remain watchful over your own heart.
The greatest battles are often unseen; the greatest victories are often unnoticed.
Blessed is the one who chooses integrity when no reward is offered; for he has become free from the slavery of applause.
Blessed is the one who does right though no eye observes him; for he has made truth his companion instead of reputation.
Such a man strengthens society without announcing himself; such a woman enriches her generation without demanding recognition.
Their reward is not merely what they accomplish; their reward is what they become.
For every deed passes away; but character remains the longest legacy a human being leaves behind.

Every nation is shaped less by its laws than by the character of those who live beneath them; for a just law in corrupt hands seldom produces justice; neither does an imperfect law prevent the righteous from doing good.

The strength of a people is first found in the strength of their conscience; a nation does not become honest because it punishes thieves; it becomes honest when fewer people desire to steal; punishment restrains the hand.
Wisdom transforms the heart; cultivate virtue before increasing penalties; the fear of prison may delay evil; only integrity persuades a man to abandon it.
Despise not the smallest decision; great rivers are gathered from small streams; great nations are gathered from ordinary citizens.
The citizen who excuses his own corruption has no authority to condemn another's; justice begins where excuses end; there are those who demand honesty from rulers while cheating their neighbors.

Such men love honesty only when it benefits them; a divided conscience cannot build an undivided nation; let every reform begin with the reformer; he who governs himself has already begun governing his society.
For example travels farther than instruction; children inherit habits more readily than speeches; teach with your life before teaching with your tongue; every household is a small nation.
The habits learned there soon become the customs of society; corruption seldom begins in parliament; it often begins in ordinary homes; truthfulness likewise begins at ordinary tables.
The future sits quietly among today's children; sow carefully; every lie planted today seeks a harvest tomorrow; every honest deed also bears fruit in its season.
The world often notices great crimes; wisdom notices the small compromises that prepared them.
A mountain is climbed one step at a time; so also is wickedness.
Resist the first invitation; small dishonesty soon asks permission for greater dishonesty.
Appetite grows by feeding; restraint grows by practice; character is formed long before it is tested.
The day of temptation merely reveals what ordinary days have built; do not wait for great trials to become honorable; become honorable in ordinary moments.
The man faithful with little seldom fears much; the man careless with little rarely stands firm in greater matters.
Integrity is not measured by the size of the decision; it is measured by the consistency of the heart.
Some men are honest only because the opportunity to deceive has not yet appeared; such honesty has not yet been tested.
Blessed is he who remains upright when advantage invites him elsewhere; the value of honesty appears most clearly when dishonesty promises reward.
Virtue without sacrifice is seldom proven; every principle eventually asks for a price.
Pay it willingly if the principle is worthy; better is temporary loss with integrity than lasting gain with shame.
Wealth acquired by abandoning the soul is expensive indeed; success purchased by self-betrayal is hidden failure.
Count not only what you gain; count also what you become while gaining it.
A full treasury cannot compensate for an empty conscience; peace is among the richest possessions.
Guard it more carefully than gold; the greedy man believes he owns his riches.
Often it is his riches that own him; every master leaves marks upon his servant.
Choose carefully what shall rule your heart; let truth be your master.
Let wisdom be your counselor; let integrity be your companion.
Let humility walk before honor; for honor pursued often escapes.
Honor deserved arrives quietly; seek not to appear great before men; seek first to become worthy of greatness, whether men notice or not.

Hypocrisy is the distance between a man's words and his life; the greater the distance, the heavier the burden he must carry; a divided life cannot produce lasting peace; for the tongue remembers one story while the hands tell another.

Better is an imperfect man who speaks honestly than a perfect image carefully maintained; reputation is borrowed from the opinions of others; character is earned in the silence of one's own choices; many labor to preserve their image.
Few labor to improve themselves; the first seeks admiration; the second seeks transformation; every man wishes to be respected.
Wisdom rewards integrity; confuse not popularity with virtue; for many celebrated men have left behind shame; and many forgotten souls have left behind honor.
Do not ask first what men admire; ask what kind of people their admiration creates; every idol quietly educates its worshippers; men eventually resemble what they continually praise.
Praise carefully; admiration is a seed; it seldom grows into anything other than itself.
The child who admires wisdom pursues understanding; the child who admires vanity pursues appearances; every generation inherits the heroes of the last.
Choose your heroes as carefully as your teachers; the feet often follow where the eyes continually look; envy disguises itself as admiration; examine the desires hidden beneath your praise.

The man who envies another's wealth seldom notices the price that purchased it; every reward has a hidden cost; every success has a story unseen by spectators; covet not the fruit before understanding the labor.
Many desire crowns; few desire the burdens beneath them; every public triumph rests upon private sacrifices; judge not the harvest before studying the seasons that produced it.
A people become what they repeatedly celebrate; celebration is never without consequence; if corruption is rewarded, corruption shall multiply; if honesty is neglected, honesty shall become rare.

If wisdom is mocked, foolishness shall become fashionable; if humility is despised, pride shall become a virtue; the future is quietly shaped by today's applause; every cheer casts a vote for tomorrow.

Be not surprised by the character of your society if you have celebrated its vices; neither despair when goodness appears, for virtue also multiplies through imitation; one honest life encourages another; one courageous act strengthens many timid hearts.
Integrity is more contagious than many believe; so also is hypocrisy; become the example you wish others to follow; the reform of a nation begins with the reform of ordinary men.
Laws restrain behavior; character transforms it; fear may produce obedience; only conviction produces integrity.
Do good not merely because someone watches; do good because goodness has become your nature.
The eye of the crowd is temporary; the witness of your conscience remains.
There are victories that enrich the purse; there are victories that enrich the soul.
Blessed is he who knows the difference; for many have gained the world they desired, only to lose the person they were becoming.
Guard your soul more carefully than your reputation; reputation belongs to others.
Your soul belongs to you; wealth may be restored after loss.
Character neglected is not so easily rebuilt; every compromise appears small when first accepted.
Yet rivers are filled one drop at a time; so also is corruption.
Great forests begin with seeds; great civilizations begin with habits.
Great men are formed by ordinary choices repeated faithfully; so also are wicked men.
The difference is seldom found in one decision alone; it is found in the direction of many.
Ask yourself each day not, "What do others think of me?"; but, "What am I becoming?".
For becoming shapes destiny more surely than appearance; blessed is the man whose private life and public voice walk the same road.

validationReportFindings.repeatedPassages:
Repeated passages in the source (kept, not removed)

These verse texts appear word-for-word in two places. They are on different pages and under different chapter numbers, with different footnotes, so this is repetition in the manuscript itself and not duplication caused by extraction. They are kept as written. The author should confirm whether the repetition is intended.

- **Society 42 and Society 43**: 29 of 30 verses identical (42:1–3 and 42:5–30 = 43:1–3 and 43:5–30). 42:4 is one of the empty references.
- **Identity 13 and Identity 14**: 28 verses identical (13:1–3, 13:5–24, 13:26–30 = 14:1–3, 14:5–24, 14:26–30). 13:4 is empty.
- **Freedom 34:23–30 and Society 41:23–30**: 8 identical verses.
- **Inquiry 41:3 = Society 41:2** and **Inquiry 41:6 = Society 41:4**.
validationReportFindings.punctuation:
Punctuation kept exactly as printed (possible typos, not corrected)

- `?;` in Inquiry 31:6 ("a life?; every"), Freedom 28:7 ("collapse?; these"), Identity 7:1 ("they are?; many")
- `.".` (full stop after a closing quotation) in Inquiry 32:3, 34:4, 39:13, Freedom 34:2, Society 41:12, and `?"; … ?".` in Identity 13:29/14:29
- Quotation marks and apostrophes are mixed: straight `'` and `"` alongside curly `’ “ ”`. Each is kept as printed.
- Dashes: verses mostly use an unspaced em dash (`word—word`). Notes mostly use a spaced one (`word — word`). Both are kept.
